summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Population growth drivers: rapid decline in death rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR), infant mortality rate (IMR), and expansion of reproductive cohort (15–49 years). Natural methods: Periodic abstinence (avoid Days 10–17), Coitus interruptus (withdrawal), and Lactational Amenorrhea (LAM, effective up to 6 months). Barrier methods: Condoms (Nirodh: only method protecting against STIs/HIV), Diaphragms, Cervical Caps, and Vaults (used with Nonoxynol-9 spermicides).

conceptBreakdown.content:
### 3.1 Population Demographics & Contraceptive Criteria
- **Population Growth Drivers**: Increased healthcare, sanitation, and medical technology have resulted in a rapid fall in the death rate, Maternal Mortality Rate (MMR), and Infant Mortality Rate (IMR), while expanding the proportion of people in the reproducible age group ($15\text{--}49\text{ years}$).
- **Criteria for an Ideal Contraceptive**: User-friendly, easily available, highly effective, completely reversible, with minimal or no side-effects, without interfering with the user's sexual drive or desire.

### 3.2 Natural / Traditional Contraceptive Modalities
1. **Periodic Abstinence (Rhythm Method)**: Couples avoid coitus from **Day 10 to Day 17** of the menstrual cycle (the Fertile Window surrounding ovulation on Day 14), when ovum and sperm viability overlap.
2. **Coitus Interruptus (Withdrawal Method)**: Male withdraws the penis from the vagina immediately prior to ejaculation to prevent insemination. *(Failure rate is high due to pre-ejaculatory bulbourethral emissions containing viable sperm)*.
3. **Lactational Amenorrhea Method (LAM)**: Intense postpartum suckling triggers high Prolactin secretion, suppressing hypothalamic GnRH and pituitary LH secretion, halting ovulation. **Effective only up to a maximum of 6 months postpartum**.

### 3.3 Barrier Contraceptive Modalities

```
                             BARRIER METHOD TYPES
                                       │
         ┌─────────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                           ▼
   CONDOMS (Male & Female)                                    CERVICAL BARRIERS
   ├── Thin rubber/latex sheaths (e.g. Nirodh)                ├── Diaphragms, Cervical Caps, Vaults
   ├── **ONLY method protecting against STIs/HIV**            ├── Reusable rubber barriers covering cervix
   └── Disposable, self-inserted, user-friendly               └── Enhanced with **Spermicidal Creams**

conceptBreakdown.heading: Pearl Index / Failure Rate
conceptBreakdown.title: Pearl Index / Failure Rate
conceptBreakdown.content: The Pearl Index measures contraceptive failure rate per 100 woman-years of exposure. Natural methods have a high Pearl Index (15-25), whereas surgical sterilization has a Pearl Index <0.1.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Nonoxynol-9 Spermicidal Surfactant Action
conceptBreakdown.title: Nonoxynol-9 Spermicidal Surfactant Action
conceptBreakdown.content: Spermicidal jellies and foams contain the non-ionic surfactant Nonoxynol-9, which rapidly intercalates into and disrupts the lipoprotein acrosomal and plasma membranes of spermatozoa, immobilizing them.
